name: ReadAgent

paper.title: A Human-Inspired Reading Agent with Gist Memory of Very Long Contexts

construction.processing: LLM chooses pause points (min/max words), then shortens each page into gist
construction.writer: backbone LLM (PaLM 2-L; GPT-3.5 in App. B)

organization.structure: flat ordered list of page-tagged gists

retrieval.selection: LLM picks raw pages to look up (parallel -P or sequential -S)
retrieval.budget: max look-up pages per task (e.g. 1-2, up to 5-6)

use.context: gists with looked-up raw pages substituted in place

stages.ingestion: Reads the long text sequentially; the LLM picks a natural pause point between min_words and max_words (episode pagination).
stages.construction: Each page is shortened by the LLM into a gist, tagged with its page number; gists are concatenated into the gist memory.
stages.organization: Ordered flat list of page gists; raw pages are kept for look-up.
stages.retrieval: The LLM reads all gists and chooses which raw pages to look up, either all at once (ReadAgent-P) or one at a time (ReadAgent-S); looked-up pages replace their gists.
stages.answer: The LLM answers from the gist memory with expanded raw pages.

summary: Prompting-only reading agent that paginates long text, keeps short gists of every page, and interactively looks up raw pages when answering.
notes:
AXES-CHECK: selection is not only reading gists - the model then retrieves raw pages (interactive look-up); '3.5-20x' in the paper is the effective context-length extension, not strictly a gist compression ratio. The paper evaluates on QuALITY, NarrativeQA, QMSum (long-document QA) and Mind2Web (web navigation) with PaLM 2-L (GPT-3.5 in App. B); no conversational-memory benchmark, so no results file was written. Code/prompts: project site read-agent.github.io.
DESIGN: Sec 3.1-3.4, Sec 4 intro. Corrected: selection is not only reading gists - LLM then retrieves raw pages; '3.5-20x' is effective context extension.
